5e83f645-340e-4327-be1e-0240c418eeb5.name: Associate Degree of Theological Studies
5e83f645-340e-4327-be1e-0240c418eeb5.description: Avondale's Associate Degree in Theological Studies (published on the live course finder under this name, sometimes listed as Associate Degree of Theological Studies) is a two year platform for studying theology, the Bible and church ministry, run out of Avondale Seminary on the Lake Macquarie campus. Students choose a combination of two disciplines from Biblical Studies, Theology and Church Ministry/Chaplaincy, and can undertake supervised field education, mentored in a local church, to gain practical ministry skills alongside the coursework. Units completed can be credited as advanced standing toward the Bachelor of Theology or the Bachelor of Ministry and Theology if a student decides to continue. Avondale is an institutional member of the Australia/New Zealand Association of Theological Studies (ANZATS) and the Australian and New Zealand Association of Theological Field Educators (ANZATFE).
5e83f645-340e-4327-be1e-0240c418eeb5.curriculum: 16 units, 96 credit points, over four semesters full time or part time equivalent. Students complete 4 units from each of two disciplines chosen from Biblical Studies (unit prefixes BBOT, BBNT, BBBI, e.g. BBNT16110 Mark and Luke, BBNT26110 NT Greek 1A, BBOT26110 Hebrew Prophets), Church Ministry/Chaplaincy (CHMN, CHPL) or Theology (THEO), plus 8 further units selected from any undergraduate unit offered by the Seminary and approved by the Course Convenor. A minimum of 4 units must be at 200 level or above. Students are encouraged to follow the first two years of the Bachelor of Ministry and Theology unit schedule to keep the option of articulating into that degree later.
5e83f645-340e-4327-be1e-0240c418eeb5.admission_requirements: A selection rank (ATAR plus adjustment factors) of at least 63, or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate uniTEST/TOWA or STAT score, for school leavers; an Australian Certificate IV (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas secondary or higher education assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1. Applicants enrolling in a CHMN or CHPL coded unit must also agree to Avondale Seminary's Code of Professional Ethics and, where relevant, provide a pastoral recommendation, a National Police Check and a Working with Children Check.
5e83f645-340e-4327-be1e-0240c418eeb5.english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-band below 6.0, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE).

b163e31e-2fb3-4e07-89ab-e31f13e88fd3.name: Bachelor of Arts
b163e31e-2fb3-4e07-89ab-e31f13e88fd3.description: Avondale's Bachelor of Arts presents the humanities and creative arts within a Christian world view, and its major list runs wider than the name suggests: alongside humanities staples (English, History, Music, Communication, Religious Studies, Visual Arts) it also carries science majors (Biological Science, Chemistry, Food and Nutrition, Mathematics) because Avondale folds those disciplines into the BA rather than running a separate standalone science degree. The course develops research, analysis, critical thinking and written and non-verbal communication skills, and is designed as both broad preparation for employment and a basis for postgraduate study.
b163e31e-2fb3-4e07-89ab-e31f13e88fd3.curriculum: 24 units, 144 credit points, over three years full time (or part time equivalent), all units worth 6 credit points unless stated otherwise. Made up of 4 Core Units (ARTS11110 The Art of Scholarship, WHPE10101 Foundations of Wellbeing, and 2 of BBUS36090 Christian Studies III, CHST26110 Studies in Christianity II, THEO36113 Religions of the World), 16 Discipline Units (a Specialisation of 12 units, a Major of 8 units, or a Minor of 4 units, chosen from Biological Science, Chaplaincy, Chemistry, Communication, English, Food and Nutrition, History, Mathematics, Music, Religious Studies or Visual Arts) and 4 Elective Units. Mathematics majors/minors need recent HSC Mathematics Extension 1 or equivalent; Music admission is by Conservatorium audition (AMEB Grade 6 performance, Grade 4 musicianship/theory, or equivalent).
b163e31e-2fb3-4e07-89ab-e31f13e88fd3.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 60 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate Avondale-approved entrance exam score, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate III (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1. Mathematics and Music majors carry additional discipline specific entry criteria (see curriculum).
b163e31e-2fb3-4e07-89ab-e31f13e88fd3.english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-band below 6.0, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE).

c95ecea3-d803-4034-9cfb-f9bf62ca33f1.name: Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Teaching (Secondary)
c95ecea3-d803-4034-9cfb-f9bf62ca33f1.description: The Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Teaching (Secondary) equips graduates to teach in Christian, independent and state high schools in Australia and overseas, with secondary teaching areas spanning Biology, Business Studies and Commerce, Chemistry, Computing Technologies, Design and Technology, English, Food Technology, Geography, Health and Physical Education, History, Home Economics, Industrial Technology, Legal Studies, Mathematics, Music, Religious Studies, Science, Technology and Applied Studies, Textiles Technology and Visual Arts. Four Professional Experience placements, including a possible overseas placement, put theory into practice across the degree. The course is available fully online for students who choose English or History/Geography as their Major/Specialisation.
c95ecea3-d803-4034-9cfb-f9bf62ca33f1.curriculum: 32 units over four years full time (or part time equivalent), combining a full BA content major (8 units) with a second teaching method area and an Education core covering areas such as curriculum and pedagogy, classroom management and assessment and reporting, plus four staged Professional Experience placements running from Year 1 observation through to a final year practicum block, meeting NSW Education Standards Authority (NESA) secondary accreditation requirements. Applicants selecting Chemistry as a teaching area need recent HSC Chemistry and Mathematics (Advanced) or equivalent; Mathematics teaching areas need HSC Mathematics Extension 1, or Mathematics Advanced plus MATH16400 General Mathematics; Music admission is by Conservatorium audition (AMEB Grade 6 performance, Grade 4 musicianship/theory, or equivalent).
c95ecea3-d803-4034-9cfb-f9bf62ca33f1.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 63 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate Avondale-approved entrance exam score, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate IV or higher (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1. All applicants must submit the Personal Statement for Initial Teacher Training (PSITE), and Chemistry, Mathematics and Music teaching areas carry additional discipline specific criteria (see curriculum).
c95ecea3-d803-4034-9cfb-f9bf62ca33f1.english_requirements: A minimum overall IELTS score of 7.5, with a minimum of 7.0 in reading and writing and a minimum of 8.0 in listening and speaking, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE), reflecting NSW teacher registration requirements.

c4a51608-dfb5-43c4-976b-3a94c1810d3f.name: Bachelor of Business
c4a51608-dfb5-43c4-976b-3a94c1810d3f.description: The Bachelor of Business at Avondale prepares students for a professional career in a business environment, with majors in Accounting, Human Resource Management, Marketing and Business Administration, plus a minor in Entrepreneurship, and its own real unit codes rather than a generic template (e.g. BBUS12010 Organisations in a Business Context, BBUS16020 Introduction to Accounting, ACCT26000 Corporate Accounting). Most students combine two majors, or a major and minor. Students are strongly encouraged to undertake an internship of at least 120 hours in a professional environment related to their area of study.
c4a51608-dfb5-43c4-976b-3a94c1810d3f.curriculum: 24 units, 144 credit points, all units worth 6 credit points. Includes 8 Business Core Units (BBUS12010 Organisations in a Business Context, BBUS16020 Introduction to Accounting, BBUS15050 Information Technology Systems in Business, BBUS16040 Introduction to Economics, BBUS14050 Business Statistics, BBUS14060 Business Law, BBUS24080 Business Finance, BBUS37400 Strategic Responses in Business), 3 Christian Studies Core units (WHPE10101 Foundations of Wellbeing, CHST26110 Studies in Christianity 2, BBUS36090 Studies in Christianity 3), and a combination of major/minor/elective units chosen from Accounting (e.g. ACCT16500 Financial Accounting and Reporting, ACCT26000 Corporate Accounting, ACCT26600 Management Accounting, ACCT31600 Accounting Theories and Practice, ACCT33400 Auditing and Assurance Services, ACCT34200 Australian Tax Law and Practice) and Business Administration (BBUS11000 Entrepreneurship, Innovation and AI Advantage, MNGT26100 Organisational Behaviour, MKTG26000 Consumer Behaviour) study patterns: two majors plus one elective, a major plus a minor plus three electives, or one major plus seven electives.
c4a51608-dfb5-43c4-976b-3a94c1810d3f.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 60 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate Avondale-approved entrance exam score, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate III (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1.
c4a51608-dfb5-43c4-976b-3a94c1810d3f.english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-band below 6.0, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE).

38beba3c-ecaa-4781-a60d-6a24d974bed6.name: Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood)(Birth - 5 Years)
38beba3c-ecaa-4781-a60d-6a24d974bed6.description: The Bachelor of Education (Early Childhood) (Birth to 5 years) equips students to teach in Christian, private, state and corporate early childhood education and care services in Australia and overseas, working within the Early Years Learning Framework and National Quality Framework. It is a highly practical degree, with 7 professional experience placements across various early childhood settings, offered both on campus and online. Graduates of this course are not eligible for primary teacher registration.
38beba3c-ecaa-4781-a60d-6a24d974bed6.curriculum: 32 units, 192 credit points, over 8 semesters of 13 weeks each (4 units per semester), studied over 4 years full time or part time equivalent. All 32 units are compulsory, with no electives, and professional experience requirements are embedded within the various EDEP (Professional Development/Experience) units across the course, building toward 7 total placements in early childhood settings.
38beba3c-ecaa-4781-a60d-6a24d974bed6.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 63 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate Avondale-approved entrance exam score, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate IV or III (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1. All applicants must complete and submit the Personal Statement for Initial Teacher Training (PSITE) for Course Convenor assessment. Applicants holding a Diploma of Early Childhood Education and Care (or higher) are eligible for a minimum of 8 units of advanced standing, with additional credit possible for approved early childhood work experience as a room leader.
38beba3c-ecaa-4781-a60d-6a24d974bed6.english_requirements: A minimum overall IELTS score of 7.5, with a minimum of 7.0 in reading and writing and a minimum of 8.0 in listening and speaking, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE), reflecting teacher registration requirements.

1032fcef-1b09-4231-84e0-7ac67343deb1.name: Bachelor of Ministry and Theology
1032fcef-1b09-4231-84e0-7ac67343deb1.description: The Bachelor of Ministry and Theology (BMinTh) is designed for those who feel called to serve as ministers of the Gospel, preparing students to serve as ministers in the church and wider community through units in church ministry, theology and biblical studies, with an optional Chaplaincy major extending career opportunities. Practical experience is built in through church placements and externships, alongside deep biblical and theological content, and Avondale is an institutional member of ANZATS and ANZATFE.
1032fcef-1b09-4231-84e0-7ac67343deb1.curriculum: 32 units, 192 credit points, over eight semesters full time (or part time equivalent), all units worth 6 credit points unless stated otherwise. Made up of Core units (2 units in Biblical Languages, 1 unit in Seventh-day Adventist History and Heritage, 1 unit in Health and Wellbeing), Discipline units (8 units each in Biblical Studies, Theology and Church Ministry, with an optional additional 8 unit Chaplaincy major making a fourth major) and 2 Elective units for students not taking the Chaplaincy major. Some Year 3 and 4 units run on a rotational calendar, and Course Convenor guidance on unit availability is recommended.
1032fcef-1b09-4231-84e0-7ac67343deb1.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 63 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate uniTEST/TOWA or STAT score, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate IV (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1. Applicants must agree to Avondale Seminary's Code of Professional Ethics, provide a satisfactory Pastoral Recommendation Form, a National Police Check and a Working with Children Check, and demonstrate active church involvement (2 years post baptism for Seventh-day Adventist applicants, or equivalent for other denominations). From 2025, all incoming theology students must also undertake psychological testing at their own expense, as recommended by the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse.
1032fcef-1b09-4231-84e0-7ac67343deb1.english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-band below 6.0, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE).

59237f9c-68d3-40fa-af32-660bcdc9935d.name: Bachelor of Nursing
59237f9c-68d3-40fa-af32-660bcdc9935d.description: Avondale's Bachelor of Nursing is ranked number one in Australia for overall experience, learner engagement, learning resources, skills development, student support and teaching quality (The Good Universities Guide 2024). Students study at either the Sydney campus, on the grounds of Sydney Adventist Hospital, or the Lake Macquarie campus, with clinical placements at hospitals including Sydney Adventist Hospital, Newcastle Private, Wyong Hospital and Gosford Public and Private Hospitals. Graduates are eligible to apply for registration as a registered nurse.
59237f9c-68d3-40fa-af32-660bcdc9935d.curriculum: 24 units, 144 credit points, over six full time semesters (or part time equivalent), including a minimum of 800 hours of professional experience. Real unit progression runs from Year 1 (NURS11101 Nursing Practice 1, NURS11103 Nursing Foundations, NURS11105 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health, NUSC11107 Applied Nursing Science 1, then NURS11102 Nursing Practice 2, NURS11104 Spiritual and Cultural Care in Nursing, NURS11106 Mental Health Nursing Foundations, NUSC11108 Applied Nursing Science 2) through Year 2 (NURS22201 to NURS22208, covering Evidence Based Nursing, Nursing Practice 3 and 4, Nursing the Older Person, Mental Health Nursing Practice, Promoting Health and Wellness, Family Health Nursing, Community Nursing Care) to Year 3 (NURS33301 to NURS33307 onward, covering Professional Roles in Nursing, Clinical Nursing Elective, Nursing Practice 5 and 6, Nursing Care for Chronic Illness, Ethics and Leadership in Nursing, Emerging Healthcare Trends), integrating physical, biological and behavioural science content throughout.
59237f9c-68d3-40fa-af32-660bcdc9935d.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 63 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate Avondale-approved entrance exam score, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate IV or higher (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1. All applicants must complete and agree to the Inherent Requirements and English Language Skills Acknowledgement. Applicants with a Diploma of Nursing completed within the last five years through an NMBA approved program may qualify for up to 8 units of advanced standing.
59237f9c-68d3-40fa-af32-660bcdc9935d.english_requirements: IELTS 7.0 overall, with a minimum of 7 in listening, reading and speaking and a minimum of 6.5 in writing, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE).

9bad8373-4500-4f0a-ac95-e3f99af46422.name: Bachelor of Theology
9bad8373-4500-4f0a-ac95-e3f99af46422.description: The Bachelor of Theology (BTheol) enables students to study biblical studies, biblical languages, theology and Christian history for personal interest or as preparation for postgraduate study and an academic career in theology. Unlike the Bachelor of Ministry and Theology, it does not prepare students for work as a pastor. Avondale is an institutional member of ANZATS and ANZATFE.
9bad8373-4500-4f0a-ac95-e3f99af46422.curriculum: 24 units, 144 credit points, over six full time semesters (or part time equivalent), all units worth 6 credit points unless stated otherwise. Core units are BBNT26110 NT Greek 1A, BBOT16110 Hebrew 1A and WHPE10101 Foundations of Wellbeing. Discipline units form an 8 unit major (5 units in Biblical Studies with at least one at 300 level, drawn from units such as BBNT16110 Mark and Luke, BBOT26110 Hebrew Prophets, BBNT36110 Exegesis of John, BBOT36110 Daniel; and 5 units in Theology with at least one at 300 level, drawn from units such as THEO16110 Theology and Faith, THEO16120 Introduction to Adventist Heritage), plus 3 further units in either Biblical Studies or Theology, a 4 unit Minor from any undergraduate course and 4 Elective units.
9bad8373-4500-4f0a-ac95-e3f99af46422.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 63 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate uniTEST/TOWA or STAT score, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate IV (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1. Applicants must agree to Avondale Seminary's Code of Professional Ethics, and those enrolling in a CHMN or CHPL coded elective must additionally provide a pastoral recommendation, National Police Check, Working with Children Check and evidence of active church involvement.
9bad8373-4500-4f0a-ac95-e3f99af46422.english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-band below 6.0, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE).

fc3078bf-65b5-4939-b95c-4a6d1d79a52b.name: Diploma of Business
fc3078bf-65b5-4939-b95c-4a6d1d79a52b.description: The Diploma of Business builds key business knowledge in accounting, human resource management, marketing and business administration for those wanting to improve general business skills for current or future employment, and doubles as a guaranteed pathway into the second year of the Avondale Bachelor of Business.
fc3078bf-65b5-4939-b95c-4a6d1d79a52b.curriculum: 8 units, 48 credit points, each unit worth 6 credit points. Semester 1: WHPE10101 Foundations of Wellbeing, BBUS12010 Organisations in a Business Context, BBUS16020 Introduction to Accounting, BBUS15050 Information Technology Systems in Business. Semester 2: BBUS16040 Introduction to Economics, BBUS14050 Business Statistics, BBUS14060 Business Law, plus one of ACCT16500 Financial Accounting and Reporting, MKTG26000 Consumer Behaviour or MNGT26100 Organisational Behaviour. Graduates enter the Bachelor of Business with credit for all eight completed units.
fc3078bf-65b5-4939-b95c-4a6d1d79a52b.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 45 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate uniTEST/TOWA or STAT score, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate III (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1.
fc3078bf-65b5-4939-b95c-4a6d1d79a52b.english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-band below 6.0, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE).

7907a1ef-be08-472b-be28-33a92003adf8.name: Diploma of Outdoor Leadership
7907a1ef-be08-472b-be28-33a92003adf8.description: SIS50421 Diploma of Outdoor Leadership is a vocational (VET) qualification delivered by Avondale (RTO 91191) that trains senior leaders to plan, lead and supervise participants in outdoor recreational activities, preparing graduates for employment in outdoor recreation, tourism and education. Most instruction takes place in the field across parts of Australia, covering activities such as bushwalking, climbing on natural surfaces, kayaking on moving water and sea kayaking. This is a physically demanding qualification, and students must be able to hike, camp and sleep outdoors, including in remote areas, and carry their own equipment.
7907a1ef-be08-472b-be28-33a92003adf8.curriculum: 28 units (13 core and 15 elective), taught over 30 weeks across 3 trimesters, with students typically attending class 3 days a week alongside self study and field based practical sessions. Core units include HLTWHS004 Manage work health and safety, SISOPLN002 Plan outdoor activity sessions, SISOPLN004 Identify hazards, assess and control risks for outdoor recreation activities, SISOPLN006 Plan for minimal environmental impact, SISXCAI006 Facilitate groups, SISXEMR002 Coordinate emergency responses, SISXIND008 Manage legal compliance in sport and recreation, PUAOPE013 Operate communications systems and equipment, SISOPLN003 Develop outdoor recreation programs, SISOPLN005 Interpret weather and environmental conditions for outdoor recreation activities, SISOPLN007 Manage risk for outdoor programs, SISXCCS002 Coordinate client service activities and SISXIND005 Coordinate work teams or groups. Electives offered at Avondale include SISOBWG003/SISOBWG007 (bushwalking in extremely difficult terrain), SISOFLD008 (navigation), SISOCLM003/006/010 (natural surface lead climbing), SISOKYK001/002/005 (flatwater and moving water kayaking) among others.
7907a1ef-be08-472b-be28-33a92003adf8.admission_requirements: Applicants should have completed SIS30619 Certificate III or SIS40621/SIS40619 Certificate IV in Outdoor Leadership, or be able to demonstrate significant outdoor leadership experience (for example through Pathfinders, Scouts, or prior outdoor recreation employment). All applicants must be 18 years or older, demonstrate Language, Literacy and Numeracy at Year 12 level or AQF 4 or higher, and provide supporting evidence (photo ID, school reports or prior qualifications), complete a literacy, language and numeracy assessment and skills assessment, an activity log, a medical form and an interview. Students must be able to obtain a Working with Children Check and meet the course's physical demands.
7907a1ef-be08-472b-be28-33a92003adf8.english_requirements: For international students, documentary evidence that secondary schooling was conducted in English with a satisfactory British O level pass or local equivalent, or an IELTS General score of at least 6.0 (or IELTS Academic 5.5) with consistent results across bands, or an equivalent approved test such as TOEFL or Cambridge Certificate in Advanced English. Other qualifications are assessed individually by the Admissions Office.

427e585c-224e-4bec-a2f4-77ef806d0d0f.name: Doctor of Philosophy
427e585c-224e-4bec-a2f4-77ef806d0d0f.description: Avondale University's Doctor of Philosophy is an internationally recognised doctoral research degree for candidates undertaking original and substantial research that advances knowledge in a chosen field, delivered within a Christian education framework with regular supervision and research training. Candidates work closely with supervisors toward a thesis typically between 80,000 and 100,000 words.
427e585c-224e-4bec-a2f4-77ef806d0d0f.curriculum: PhD candidates design, plan and execute a supervised research project addressing a gap identified in their literature review, resulting in a written thesis, a combination of written exegesis and creative performance, or a thesis by publication, tracked against key milestones. Candidates enrol in DPHL71000 Doctor of Philosophy Thesis throughout candidature until thesis submission, then DPHL72000 Doctor of Philosophy Thesis, Under Examination. Standard candidature is 3 to 3.5 years full time (or part time equivalent), with a maximum of 4 years full time (or part time equivalent).
427e585c-224e-4bec-a2f4-77ef806d0d0f.admission_requirements: Completion of an Australian master's research degree, or an Australian bachelor's degree with First or Second Class Division A Honours including a minimum 25 percent research component, or an Australian master's coursework degree with a minimum overall GPA of 5.5 on a 7 point scale and a minimum 25 percent research component, or an Australian professional doctoral degree with a minimum 25 percent research component, or a comparable or higher overseas qualification. Applicants must submit certified academic transcripts, a detailed research proposal using Avondale's HDR Research Proposal template, a CV and two written academic references, and acceptance depends on alignment with one of Avondale's Research Centres and the availability of suitable supervisors.
427e585c-224e-4bec-a2f4-77ef806d0d0f.english_requirements: A minimum overall Academic IELTS score of 7.0 with no sub-band below 7.0, or a qualification Avondale deems equivalent, or documentary evidence of a prior qualification taught and assessed in English within the last two years in a recognised English speaking country.

a65f8214-ad2f-431a-8448-21879f0774b9.name: Master of Arts
a65f8214-ad2f-431a-8448-21879f0774b9.description: Avondale's Master of Arts equips Christian leaders for greater effectiveness in ministry within a church, school, hospital or the wider community, engaging students in advanced ministerial and theological studies and the application of research to new ministry contexts. It is offered with a specialisation in Pastoral Leadership, Chaplaincy Studies, Theology/Biblical Studies, or Youth and Family Ministry (Chaplaincy Studies and Youth and Family Ministry are subject to sufficient cohort numbers).
a65f8214-ad2f-431a-8448-21879f0774b9.curriculum: 12 units, 72 credit points, studied part time over 4 years (generally three units per year), all units worth 6 credit points unless stated otherwise. 3 core units (CMIN51100 Graduate Studies in Biblical Spirituality, THBB56600 Theology, Theory and Practice of Leadership for Ministry, CMIN52110 Discipleship and Disciple making) plus 5 specialisation units (e.g. Pastoral Leadership: THBB54100 Perspectives on Luke-Acts, THBB56500 Theology of Mission; Chaplaincy Studies: CHPL41500 Fundamentals of Counselling for Chaplains, CMIN56500 Clinical Pastoral Education 1, which includes 400 hours of approved clinical work) and either 4 electives, or 2 electives plus THRE51000 Research Project (6 credit points, 5000 words), or a research methods unit plus THRE52000 Extended Research Project (18 credit points, 15000 words). Students can exit with a Graduate Certificate in Arts after 4 units or a Graduate Diploma in Arts after 8 units. The New South Wales College of Clinical Pastoral Education accredits the clinical pastoral education units.
a65f8214-ad2f-431a-8448-21879f0774b9.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor of Ministry and/or Theology or equivalent, or Avondale's Graduate Certificate in Arts, or an overseas ministry or theology qualification comparable to an Australian Bachelor's degree or higher. Applicants for the Youth and Family Ministry or Chaplaincy specialisation may instead hold a Bachelor in Chaplaincy with a major in Theology, or a Bachelor of Education or Teaching with a major in Religious Studies, as approved by the Course Convenor. Applicants need at least two years of ministry or chaplaincy experience and current or recent employment in the field, plus a 250 word written summary of that experience and their reasons for enrolling.
a65f8214-ad2f-431a-8448-21879f0774b9.english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-band below 6.0, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE), or documentary evidence of a prior qualification (or at least two years of tertiary study) taught and assessed in English within the last two years in a recognised English speaking country.

c2e98bc9-488d-498a-a776-64bc7791a218.name: Master of Education
c2e98bc9-488d-498a-a776-64bc7791a218.description: Avondale's Master of Education is built for working teachers, delivered entirely online except for a single annual Winter School (one week each July) on the Lake Macquarie campus. It has four specialisation options, Leadership and Administration, Special and Inclusive Education, Curriculum and Teaching, and Health and Wellbeing, or can be completed without a specialisation. Units are recognised as accredited Professional Development by all Australian state teacher accreditation authorities, contributing 50 hours each toward maintenance requirements.
c2e98bc9-488d-498a-a776-64bc7791a218.curriculum: 8 units, 48 credit points, part time only, all units worth 6 credit points unless stated otherwise. Made up of 1 core Christian education unit (EDUC50400 Worldviews and Value Issues in Christian Education, or EDUC50600 School as a Caring Community), the compulsory EDUC50000 Introduction to Educational Research, a research project unit (EDUR59200 Independent Project 6 CP, EDUR59300 Extended Independent Project 12 CP, or EDUR59400 Major Educational Research Project 18 CP) and 3 to 5 specialisation or elective units. Specialisation units are drawn from named lists, for example Leadership and Administration (LAMC50600 Theology, Theory and Practice of Leadership, LAMC51400 Human Resource Management, EDUC56100 School Effectiveness) or Special and Inclusive Education (EDUC55500 to EDUC55800, covering inclusion strategies, issues and educational approaches, gifted and talented, and specific learning disabilities).
c2e98bc9-488d-498a-a776-64bc7791a218.admission_requirements: An Australian four year Bachelor's degree in Education, a Bachelor's degree followed by a Diploma of Education, a Bachelor of Teaching, an Australian Graduate Certificate in Educational Studies, an Australian Master of Teaching, or a comparable overseas qualification. Applicants must also submit a resume or written summary (maximum 2 pages) showing at least two years of relevant work experience.
c2e98bc9-488d-498a-a776-64bc7791a218.english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.5 with no sub-band below 7.0, or a recognised alternative under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE), or documentary evidence of a prior qualification taught and assessed in English within the last two years in a recognised English speaking country.

b766e2a3-8046-467c-873d-56f8b8fc9bf6.name: Master of Ministry
b766e2a3-8046-467c-873d-56f8b8fc9bf6.description: The Master of Ministry (MMin) is a professional graduate program for those who already hold a degree in another discipline and feel called to serve as ministers of the Gospel. It integrates biblical knowledge with practical experience, including church placements and an externship, and can be studied on campus or online. Avondale is an institutional member of ANZATS and ANZATFE.
b766e2a3-8046-467c-873d-56f8b8fc9bf6.curriculum: 16 units, 96 credit points, over four full time semesters (or part time equivalent), all units worth 6 credit points unless stated otherwise, maximum 8 years to complete. Units include BBNT46110 Greek, BBOT46110 Pentateuch in Context, BBNT56130 Gospels of Matthew and John, BBBI56110 Daniel and the Apocalypses, BBNT56120 New Testament Epistles, THEO46110 Theology and Belief, THEO56140 Eschatology and Salvation, THEO56120 Adventist Heritage, THEO56150 Ecclesiology and Doctrine of the Sabbath, THEO46230 Church History, CHMN56150 World Mission and Evangelism, CHMN46160 Family Systems in Ministry, CHMN46110 Church and Ministry, CHMN56140 Biblical Preaching, CHMN46130 Personal Evangelism and Discipleship and CHMN56180 Pastoral Leadership and Church Management, with study running across a recommended even year or odd year commencement pattern and church placements and an externship embedded throughout.
b766e2a3-8046-467c-873d-56f8b8fc9bf6.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor's degree or higher, or a comparable overseas qualification. Applicants must provide a satisfactory Pastoral Recommendation Form completed by their church pastor, agree to Avondale Seminary's Code of Professional Ethics, provide a National Police Check and a Working with Children Check, and demonstrate active church involvement (2 years post baptism for Seventh-day Adventist applicants, or equivalent for other denominations). From 2025, all incoming theology students must also undertake psychological testing at their own expense, as recommended by the Royal Commission into Institutional Responses to Child Sexual Abuse.
b766e2a3-8046-467c-873d-56f8b8fc9bf6.english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-band below 6.0, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE), or documentary evidence of a prior qualification taught and assessed in English within the last two years in a recognised English speaking country.

5f2a8337-5d5c-4528-8248-091e338a7e21.name: Master of Philosophy
5f2a8337-5d5c-4528-8248-091e338a7e21.description: Avondale's Master of Philosophy is an internationally recognised research degree for candidates undertaking a supervised research project that contributes to knowledge in a chosen field, delivered within a Christian education framework with regular supervision and research training. Candidates work toward a thesis of approximately 40,000 to 60,000 words and the degree provides a pathway to doctoral study.
5f2a8337-5d5c-4528-8248-091e338a7e21.curriculum: MPhil candidates design, plan and execute a supervised research project, resulting in a written thesis, a combination of written exegesis and creative performance, or a thesis by publication, tracked against key milestones. Candidates enrol in MPHL61000 Master of Philosophy Thesis throughout candidature until submission, then MPHL62000 Master of Philosophy Thesis, Under Examination. Minimum candidature is 1 year full time, expected 1.5 years full time, maximum 2 years full time (part time equivalent throughout).
5f2a8337-5d5c-4528-8248-091e338a7e21.admission_requirements: Completion of an Australian Bachelor's degree with a minimum overall GPA of 5 on a 7 point scale (or equivalent), or an Australian Master's by coursework degree, or a comparable or higher overseas qualification. Applicants must submit certified academic transcripts, a detailed research proposal using Avondale's HDR Research Proposal template, a CV and two written academic references, and acceptance depends on alignment with one of Avondale's Research Centres and the availability of suitable supervisors.
5f2a8337-5d5c-4528-8248-091e338a7e21.english_requirements: A minimum overall Academic IELTS score of 7.0 with no sub-band below 7.0, or a qualification Avondale deems equivalent, or documentary evidence of a prior qualification taught and assessed in English within the last two years in a recognised English speaking country.

061aa911-959d-45e1-baf1-6da26a2d4fe3.name: Master of Teaching (Primary)
061aa911-959d-45e1-baf1-6da26a2d4fe3.description: The Master of Teaching (Primary) is for graduates who already hold a bachelor's degree and want to move into primary school teaching, qualifying graduates to teach in Christian, independent and state school systems in Australia and overseas. It includes 60 days of Professional Experience, and is offered either as a regular semester only program or a fast tracked 1.3 year program with online intensive study periods.
061aa911-959d-45e1-baf1-6da26a2d4fe3.curriculum: 16 units, 96 credit points, over 4 semesters full time (or part time equivalent), each unit worth 6 credit points. Made up of 15 Education units (7 Core Education units, including EDUC50102 Understanding Students with Special Education Needs, EDUC50113 Exploring Indigenous Education, EDUC52102 Introduction to Learning and Teaching, EDUC52103 Managing the Primary Classroom; and 8 Curriculum and Pedagogical Studies units, including EDUC14102 Curriculum Studies, Teaching English I, EDUC14105 Curriculum Studies, Teaching Mathematics I, EDUC24107 Curriculum Studies, Teaching Science and Technology, EDUC54102 Curriculum Studies, Primary Creative Arts) plus 1 Professional Experience unit, EDPX30001. Two professional experience placement blocks total 60 days: a 20 consecutive day block in July to August, and a 40 consecutive day block either mid Year 2 (regular program) or at the end of the fast tracked program.
061aa911-959d-45e1-baf1-6da26a2d4fe3.admission_requirements: An Australian Bachelor's degree (or higher) that meets NSW Education Standards Authority (NESA) content requirements as assessed by the Course Convenor, or a comparable overseas qualification. Applicants must submit the Personal Statement for Initial Teacher Training (PSITE) and must have achieved a Band 4 result in HSC Mathematics, or completed 1 unit of mathematics/numeracy in a prior undergraduate degree, or enrol in a bridging mathematics/numeracy unit.
061aa911-959d-45e1-baf1-6da26a2d4fe3.english_requirements: A minimum overall IELTS score of 7.5, with a minimum of 7.0 in reading and writing and a minimum of 8.0 in listening and speaking, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE), or documentary evidence of a prior qualification taught and assessed in English within the last two years in a recognised English speaking country.

8d174843-5552-4c4b-ba6f-5b4d9ee1c77c.name: Undergraduate Certificate in Business
8d174843-5552-4c4b-ba6f-5b4d9ee1c77c.description: The Undergraduate Certificate in Business is a condensed 4 unit introduction to key principles and practices in business, covering accounting, marketing, human resource management, information technology and business communication, aimed at entry level roles or as a stepping stone into further business study. Completion guarantees direct entry into the second semester of the Avondale Diploma of Business or Bachelor of Business.
8d174843-5552-4c4b-ba6f-5b4d9ee1c77c.curriculum: 4 units, 24 credit points, over 1 semester full time (or part time equivalent), maximum 1 year to complete. Semester 1: BBUS12010 Organisations in a Business Context, BBUS16020 Introduction to Accounting, BBUS15050 Information Technology Systems in Business, BBUS11000 Entrepreneurship, Innovation and AI Advantage. Semester 2: BBUS16040 Introduction to Economics, BBUS14050 Business Statistics, BBUS14060 Business Law, plus one of ACCT16500 Financial Accounting and Reporting, MKTG26000 Consumer Behaviour, MNGT26100 Organisational Behaviour or MKTG28100 Marketing Communication. Completed units may provide credit for the same units in the Diploma of Business or Bachelor of Business.
8d174843-5552-4c4b-ba6f-5b4d9ee1c77c.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 45 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate Avondale-approved entrance exam score, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate III approved by the Course Convenor (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1.
8d174843-5552-4c4b-ba6f-5b4d9ee1c77c.english_requirements: IELTS 6.5 overall with no sub-band below 6.0, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE).

8160389a-4c56-486d-b42c-7d60c7019521.name: Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation
8160389a-4c56-486d-b42c-7d60c7019521.description: The Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation is a free tertiary pathway course for school leavers with no ATAR, or who have not achieved an entry level ATAR, and for mature aged students seeking an alternate entry into a bachelor's degree. With one on one support, students develop tertiary literacy, written, verbal and communication skills and general academic skills to prepare for university study.
8160389a-4c56-486d-b42c-7d60c7019521.curriculum: 4 units, 24 credit points, over 1 semester full time (or part time equivalent), on campus or online (noting Nursing units are not offered online). Students commencing in Semester 1 enrol in WHPE10101 Foundations of Wellbeing, ARTS11110 The Art of Scholarship, plus 2 elective units, selectable from 100 level units across Teaching, Arts, Business, Ministry and Theology (with partial credit into Nursing) to maximise credit transfer into a student's planned degree.
8160389a-4c56-486d-b42c-7d60c7019521.admission_requirements: A selection rank of at least 45 (ATAR plus adjustment factors), or 24 points in the IB Diploma, or NZ Year 13 NCEA Level 3 university entrance, or an appropriate Avondale-approved entrance exam score, or a Senior Secondary Certificate with no ATAR, for school leavers not currently in Year 12; an Australian Certificate III (or equivalent NZ certificate) for VET entrants; at least 2 completed Bachelor's units, a bridging/enabling course, or 3 completed units of Avondale's Undergraduate Certificate in University Preparation for those who have already attended university; overseas qualifications assessed under Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) Appendix 1.
8160389a-4c56-486d-b42c-7d60c7019521.english_requirements: The IELTS score required for the specific course the applicant plans to study after completing this Undergraduate Certificate, or an equivalent pathway listed in Appendix 2 of Avondale's Admission Policy (HE) for that course.
